title: chatv1-coexistence-layer-stream-coalescer-and-tool-fallthrough
author: Ayesha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a compatibility coexistence layer for /v1/chat.completions clients, improves streaming stability with a stream coalescer, and introduces a tool fallthrough policy to avoid silent tool-call drops. No breaking changes for existing Redwood API users; OpenAI-compat clients may observe more stable streaming and clearer function-call envelopes.
description: Motivation: customer integrations and internal SDKs have hit intermittent failures and duplicated fragments when simultaneously supporting Redwood native streaming and the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility path. This PR introduces a coexistence layer to reliably translate and normalize parameters and streaming frames between both paths, a stream coalescer to reduce fragment duplication and reordering, and a configurable tool fallthrough policy so function/tool calls that cannot be routed to a registered tool surface predictable structured output instead of being dropped. Changes include protocol-level canonicalization for roles/stop/logprobs, a logprob reconciliation pass to fill missing probabilities when upstream models omit them, and a structured-json-envelope canonicalizer for downstream SDKs.

- [x] Add tool fallthrough policy and default of 'structured-fallback' for v1 clients -- runtime/tooling/fallthrough.go
- [x] Reconcile stop-signal priority between internal StopSet and OpenAI stop array semantics
- [x] Add unit + integration tests across Python and TS SDKs; add canary in perf-lab
- [x] Update docs and OpenAI-compat examples
- [x] Run full regression suite and iterate on CI failures until green

notes_for_maintainers: - Coexistence adapter lives under server/api/openai_compat to keep coupling low. If we later deprecate v1 compatibility, remove adapter and fallthrough policy.
upgrade_impact: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions clients should see more stable streaming and clearer structured fallback when tools are missing. Operators can tune the coalescer via runtime.stream.coalescer.* flags in release notes. No action required for Redwood native API users.
